approach:
Root cause, worded identically in new decision D189 and in the CHANGELOG entry: criteria are checked independently only after the producer ends, so an unmet criterion found by the verifier cannot trigger a repair. `produce_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1871-1950) runs one producer loop, one candidate, one set of checks and one verifier, and a fail verdict closes the job Rejected. Only the producer's own report is ever sent back (`unmet_criteria`, run/send_back.rs:19, used at producer.rs:465). What is missing is the independent verdict reaching the producer while a round is left to use it. Fix, in the run pipeline, bounded, with no refusal rule (0% of past accepted readings newly refused).

(a) `produce_and_verify` keeps baseline and the disk gate once and moves one round (snapshot, producer loop, candidate, remove work tree, `Built`, resume mark, `check_and_verify`) into `produce_round(.., seed, repair)`.

(b) After round one, a pure `verify::repair_view(&Verification) -> Option<RepairView>` reads the stored verdict. It is Some only when the verifier judged (`agent_verdict` Some), the final verdict is Fail and a repairable item is left: an unmet criterion or a blocker or major finding, after dropping the kinds a producer cannot change: a criterion the verifier did not assess, a request misread, and (finding 6, new rule) the Athena D43 items only when the verifier's own verdict was Pass, because then Athena alone flipped them. With the verifier's verdict Fail the D43 items stay in, since the stored record cannot tell Athena's flip from the verifier's own unmet.

(c) While fewer than the new `VERIFIER_REPAIRS` (=1, beside `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, mod.rs:1681) repairs have run, not nested, and `preflight(Run)` and the disk gate pass, it clones round one's candidate, verification, happened state and `files`, writes the first-round items into the first verifier invocation's `detail`, removes the job's resume mark, and runs round two from a snapshot seeded with the first candidate (`SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`, producer.rs:144-153). Round two's brief comes from `send_back_text_repaired`, the new last link of the existing send-back chain, and the same view goes into `producer_loop`, so round two's own send-back keeps one `## Sent back` heading.

(d) If round two reaches a verdict, it is final and a fail names all first-round items in the closing reason. If round two returns Ok with no Verification (producer stop, deadline, expired login, admission, gate, scope or check-timeout stop), round one's candidate, Verification, happened state AND files are restored, round two's kept-work directory is removed, and the job closes Rejected: exactly where it would have closed without the repair, plus round two's stop reason and the repair note in the reason. If round two returns an error (a hold), `commit_hold` keeps its existing behaviour.

Answers to the revision's findings:
- Findings 1 and 2 (minor, files outside the deliverables): kept, as two one-purpose edits. `finding_text` is `pub(super)` at reading/retry.rs:446 and reaches the crate only if widened (`pub use retry::*;` at reading.rs:70 re-exports it); the other way is a second copy in verify.rs that drifts from the retry brief. The drain test at drain.rs:5204 counts producer entries and breaks when a failing verdict repairs; `cargo test --locked` is recorded check 6, so it must change. The request's Files is `crates/`.
- Finding 3 (major): no `format!` literal in `judge` is edited or moved. The D43 literal (verify.rs:602) and the not-assessed literal (552) stay in place, so `drift_haystack` (verify.rs:3881-3920, which reads only `//!` header lines and `format!(` literals between `\npub fn judge(` and the next `\n}\n`) and the tests at 3923-3945 see the same text. Only two non-`format!` literals become shared consts used by `judge` and `repair_view` (the not-assessed evidence at 544 and the misread summary at 631); `drift_haystack` does not scan them (3896). `repair_view` recognises the two `format!` findings by shared prefix and suffix consts, and a test with the real `judge` pins each recogniser to what `judge` writes.
- Finding 4 (minor): `FirstRound` also holds the closing's files, and the restore puts them back, so round two's `progress-note.md` (mod.rs:1008) is gone. The restore also calls `remove_kept_work(&id)` (state.rs:115) for the directory `keep_unfinished_work` may have moved (mod.rs:988-998). An environment stop or deadline in round two is classed as the first verdict, Rejected, and not as an environment stop. Without the repair the same job would already have closed Rejected after round one, so no attempt is newly used and nothing resumable is lost: Rejected is never resumable (`resumable_stop`, disk.rs:537-543; `keeps_unfinished_work`, disk.rs:549-557). `settle_resume_marks` (mod.rs:886) removes the mark for a Rejected job. D189 says so, and the stop test gains a deadline case and an expired-login case.
- Finding 5 (minor): same restore of `files`: round one's replay record and `brief-verifier.md` come back. The only three writers of `closing.files` before close are mod.rs:1008, mod.rs:2264-2268 and verification.rs:201, and I read close.rs:135, 272 and 636 as readers or close-time extenders. A direct unit test of the restore proves the files come back whatever stop point is hit.
- Finding 6 (minor): taken as the first option: D43 items stay repairable when the verifier's verdict is Fail and are dropped only when it is Pass; tests pin both. The cost, a repair round that the producer cannot always change, is bounded to one round and named in D189 and the CHANGELOG as unmeasured.

decisions.choice: Repair loop wraps one round in `produce_and_verify`; the trigger is the pure `verify::repair_view` over the stored `Verification`, not a new field carried out of `verification_stage`.
decisions.reason: Everything the trigger needs is already stored: `agent_verdict` is Some exactly when the verifier returned output (verify.rs:639-645), a timeout or incomplete verifier leaves it None, and `Finding.source` and `CriterionResult.evidence` carry what is needed to spot Athena's own findings (verify.rs:292-299, 541-555, 600-604, 629-633). Reusing the whole round keeps admission, the decision gate, the checks, the replay and the pull-request replace identical for the second candidate. A `closing.verification` that is Some after round two means a verdict was reached, because round one's is taken out before round two and the early stops in `check_and_verify` (mod.rs:1979-2056) and the `candidate_stage` stops return with it None. Existing code already treats a misread and an unmet or unseen Behavior criterion as not retryable from the tree (`qualifies_for_tree_retry`, retry.rs:347-359), so the exclusions match what the repo already means by 'a producer pass cannot fix it'.

rejected.option: Set a typed `Closing.repair` inside `verification_stage`
rejected.why: Adds plumbing and a second copy of what the stored Verification already holds; the pure function is tested with the real `judge`.

rejected.option: Re-run only the verifier with a producer pass inside `verification_stage`
rejected.why: It has no producer snapshot, grant or prompt and would skip candidate, admission and checks for the repaired tree.

rejected.option: Raise PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS and send back on the producer's own report
rejected.why: That is the self-report direction the dropped jobs took; the failing signal is the independent verdict, which exists only after verification.

rejected.option: Edit role prompts to tell the producer to check each criterion
rejected.why: Out of scope: those prompt, budget and wrapping edits were dropped with jobs 20261014-170031-2r9b, -172342-rqgb and -174937-hrzn.

decisions.choice: New `const VERIFIER_REPAIRS: u32 = 1` beside `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, enforced by a counter. No repair for a nested run, a resumed candidate, a failed `preflight(Run)` or low disk (one `repair     skipped: ...` line for the last two). Before round two starts the job's resume mark is removed (`remove_resume`, state.rs:315).
decisions.reason: The bound is in code and named (criterion 5). `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` is documented as the shared pre-verifier send-back (mod.rs:1677-1681) and D182 keeps it at 1, so it is not reused. `preflight(Run)` (reading.rs:502-515; reserve = producer + verifier caps) means no repair starts that the job budget cannot pay; the live athena.toml has producer 10.00, verifier 5.00 and job 50.00 (lines 45-47), so a normal job can pay. A nested run is judged by the outer job, the same guard as mod.rs:1980, 2006, 2028. `resume_candidate` (mod.rs:843-844) calls `check_and_verify` directly and never reaches the loop. Round one writes a resume mark for the first candidate (mod.rs:1948) and `settle_resume_marks` keeps a mark only for a Failed environment stop (mod.rs:886); without removal, a round-two hold or stop would let `athena retry` resume the already-rejected first candidate with no repair. Removing it first means a hold before round two's candidate is admitted leaves no mark (the documented pre-producer hold, close.rs:170-176), and once round two's candidate is admitted `produce_round` writes a mark that points at round two's candidate.

rejected.option: Reuse PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 2
rejected.why: It would give the producer's own report two send-backs and change every send-back test and D182.

rejected.option: Unbounded repair until the verifier passes
rejected.why: Unbounded cost; the reading says one round.

rejected.option: Hold the job for low disk before round two
rejected.why: A hold before a producer means no candidate yet (close.rs:170-176), so the first verdict would be thrown away; skipping keeps the first verdict.

rejected.option: Leave round one's resume mark in place
rejected.why: A retry would resume the first, already rejected candidate with no repair.

decisions.choice: Store the repair as ordinary records, with no new record type or field. Keep a `FirstRound { candidate, verification, happened, files }` clone while round two runs, and restore all four when round two returns Ok with no Verification (state Rejected, `verification_passed` Some(false), round two's kept-work directory removed). A hold (Err) is left to `commit_hold` as it is.
decisions.reason: `candidate_stage` sets `closing.candidate` to round two's candidate on its paths (candidate.rs:178, 220, 227) and each stop replaces `closing.happened` through `self.failure` (state Failed, mod.rs:2581-2591), and `keep_unfinished_work` adds a progress note (mod.rs:1008) and may move the work tree (mod.rs:988-998). Without the restore a repaired job whose second producer fails would close Failed with no Verification, and `tree_retry_seed` returns None without one (retry.rs:410-412). The restore also covers findings 4 and 5: `closing.files` is written before close only at mod.rs:1008 (progress note), mod.rs:2264-2268 (replay record) and verification.rs:201 (`brief-verifier.md`), so restoring the cloned `files` removes the stale note and puts round one's replay and verifier brief back. Round two's invocations stay in `new_invocations`. With the restore the job ends where it ended before this change: Rejected with the first candidate and verifier findings, so `qualifies_for_tree_retry` (retry.rs:330-370) and `tree_retry_seed` (retry.rs:392-443) see round one. Classing: a deadline, expired login, usage limit, check timeout or any producer, admission, gate or scope stop in round two is the first verdict standing, not an environment stop; this uses no attempt that the first verdict had not already used. `Closing::put_file` (remove same-path files, then push) is used for the replay record and `brief-verifier.md` so a round that reaches a verdict replaces round one's. Round one's verifier `Invocation.detail` lists every unmet criterion and blocking finding (no count cap, each item clipped to 240 chars) and says the work was sent back for one repair pass. When round two reaches a verdict, a fail has reason `the final verdict is fail: {second reasons}. {note}`; a restored first round has `the final verdict is fail: {first reasons}. {note}; the repair pass stopped before a verdict: {round two's stop reason}`. The prefix `the final verdict is fail:` stays first (close.rs:53); the note is redacted with the job's redactor. `Happened`, `Candidate`, `Verification` and `NewFile` are Clone (commits.rs:18-22). The introspector builds `what` from `outcome.reason` plus `failure_details(verification)` and does not read `Invocation.detail` (introspect.rs:1538-1572), so the reason carries all first-round items.

rejected.option: Take round one's Verification out and leave it out when round two stops
rejected.why: The job would close Failed with no Verification and a retry would lose the first candidate and the verifier's blocking findings.

rejected.option: Restore only candidate, verification and happened state
rejected.why: Leaves round two's progress note, kept-work directory and, after put_file, round two's replay and verifier brief beside round one's Verification (findings 4 and 5).

rejected.option: Keep an environment stop in round two as an environment stop and resume from round two's kept work
rejected.why: The first verdict would be lost and the job would hold a candidate with no Verification; a Rejected close equals today's outcome and the retry then seeds from the first candidate and findings.

rejected.option: Keep both Verification records
rejected.why: The path is per job (records.rs:934); a second would overwrite it or need a new path and an allow-list change in athena-data.

rejected.option: Add a typed `repair` field to Invocation or Verification
rejected.why: It changes athena-data record shapes and every stored-record reader for information the detail and reason text already carry.

rejected.option: Push the repair note into `Verification.reasons`
rejected.why: It would put a reason on a passing verification and change what the landing gate and `verified()` see.

rejected.option: Cap the note at 3 items
rejected.why: A first round with four or more items would again leave an unmet criterion out of the stored event, the failure class being fixed.

decisions.choice: The repair brief extends the existing builder chain: `send_back_text_scoped` becomes a wrapper over a new last link `send_back_text_repaired(.., repair: Option<&RepairView>)`, and the same `Option<&RepairView>` is passed into `producer_loop`, which uses it for its first attempt brief and for its own send-backs (the four-arm match at producer.rs:684-700 becomes one call). With None the text is byte-identical. With Some, one `## Sent back` heading holds the repair intro (it replaces the 'Your previous report...' paragraph) then the lists.
decisions.reason: The shared intro is false for a repair: 'your previous report did not show every criterion met', 'This is the only send-back' and 'A run that leaves no change fails' (send_back.rs:162-173); a seeded run that adds nothing is the candidate, not an idle producer (candidate.rs:168-181). The base snapshot text says 'a snapshot of the base commit's files' (briefs.rs:710-714) while the seeded one is the base plus the candidate's files laid over it, uncommitted (snapshot.rs:97-101). The intro states four facts: the directory is a fresh snapshot already holding the first candidate (`git diff` against its base shows it); the independent verifier, not the producer's report, found the items; a run that adds nothing keeps the first candidate and it is verified again unchanged; the verdict after this round is final. `producer_loop` builds its own send-back from the `brief` it is given (producer.rs:684-700), so if round two's brief were already a repair text the result would hold two `## Sent back` headings; passing the view in keeps one heading, and items from the producer's own report in this round are listed under the existing headings after the repair intro (`append_mirror_drift`, send_back.rs:227-247, still finds one heading). The findings block is shared with `must_address_block` (briefs.rs:616-629) and each finding is formatted by `finding_text` (retry.rs:446), so a finding reads the same in a retry and in a repair; texts pass through `ctx.redactor` as `tree_retry_seed` does (retry.rs:424).

rejected.option: A separate `repair_brief` function
rejected.why: A parallel builder, contrary to criterion 5.

rejected.option: Only prepend one sentence to the shared intro
rejected.why: The rest of that intro would stay false.

rejected.option: Build round two's brief as a repair text and let `producer_loop` nest its own send-back under it
rejected.why: Two `## Sent back` headings and contradicting sentences.

rejected.option: A new formatter for findings in briefs.rs
rejected.why: It would describe the same finding differently from the retry brief.

decisions.choice: Trigger and exclusions in `repair_view`: a judged Fail verdict with an unmet criterion or a blocker or major finding, minus (i) a criterion whose evidence is the not-assessed text and its Athena 'Criterion N was not assessed' finding; (ii) the Athena request-misread finding; (iii) only when `agent_verdict` is Pass, the Athena D43 findings ('Behavior criterion N is unmet: ... must cite commands that ran (D43)') and the criteria they name. With `agent_verdict` Fail the D43 items stay in. The recognisers are shared consts in verify.rs (`NOT_ASSESSED_EVIDENCE`, `MISREAD_SUMMARY`, `NOT_ASSESSED_SUFFIX`, `D43_PREFIX`, `D43_SUFFIX`); `judge` uses the first two for its non-`format!` literals and keeps both `format!` literals where they are.
decisions.reason: `judge` fails the verdict on exactly these items (verify.rs:646-664). Not-assessed (verify.rs:549-555) and misread (627-634) describe what the verifier did or read, and nothing a producer pass changes decides them. The D43 flip sets `met = false` where the verifier's cited commands were not seen running or it cited none (585-605), and the stored record loses the verifier's own `met`. When the verifier's verdict is Pass every unmet or blocking D43 item is Athena's flip, so a producer pass cannot fix it. When it is Fail the verifier itself found a fault, often in that same criterion (for example 'a test fails without the change' with no such test), so the repair runs. The known cost: a Fail whose only serious items are D43 flips spends one round the producer may not be able to change; bounded to one round, not measured, named in D189 and the CHANGELOG. A failing check repairs only through the verifier: `judge` adds a Minor finding for a failing check (verify.rs:448-473) and the check blocks a pass at verify.rs:663, so a verdict that marks the check criterion unmet, or adds a blocker or major finding, repairs; a failing check that the verifier did not flag triggers none. Athena's own blockers and majors that a producer can fix (held replay, a requirement row marked Covered) stay in. Keeping the `format!` literals inside `judge` leaves `drift_haystack` (verify.rs:3881-3920) and its tests (3923-3945) unchanged.

rejected.option: Trigger on every blocker or major finding
rejected.why: Repairs a misread or an unassessed criterion at full cost with no way to change the outcome.

rejected.option: Trigger on a failed check as well
rejected.why: The producer already had one send-back with the check's output tail before the verifier; the verifier's unmet check criterion already triggers a repair.

rejected.option: Exclude all D43 items (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Misses a criterion the verifier itself judged unmet and that cites no command; `agent_verdict` Fail is a stored signal that narrows the gap.

rejected.option: Move the D43 and not-assessed `format!` strings into `d43_summary`/`not_assessed_summary` functions outside `judge`
rejected.why: `rule_sources_appear_in_the_header_or_judge_format_strings` (verify.rs:3923-3937) would fail: it needs 'must cite commands that ran (D43)' inside a `format!` literal in `judge`.

rejected.option: Exclude check criteria (`is_athena_check_criterion`) from the trigger
rejected.why: A failing fmt, clippy or test check is a producer-fixable cause and the most common unmet criterion in the 43 introspections.

Split `produce_and_verify` into `produce_round` plus the one-repair loop (guards, first-verifier detail, `repair` UI lines, resume-mark removal, kept-work removal and restore on a round with no verdict, reason note). Push `brief-verifier.md` through `closing.put_file` (line 201) so a second round replaces it. No verdict logic changes.

risks.risk: Many existing tests (run/tests.rs, athena-cli) use a fixed failing verdict and assume one producer and one verifier run, so the blast radius is larger than the 11 listed deliverables.
risks.mitigation: Step 11 runs the whole workspace suite right after the core change, so the real list is found by `cargo test --locked`. Each assertion that counted one round for a failing verdict gets new counts, costs or a script answer for the second call. I read drain.rs:5204 and expect it to change; lifecycle.rs:641-731 and introspection.rs:421-471 should pass because the retry brief reads only the final Verification and `what` still holds the final verification's items. Athena flags files outside the listed deliverables as minor and the plan accepts that.

risks.risk: Cost: a repaired job pays for a second producer pass, checks (with their timeouts) and verifier, and holds the build-folder slot one round longer. With D43 items repairable on a verifier Fail, some repairs may be rounds the producer cannot change.
risks.mitigation: The bound is a named constant, tested at exactly one repair. `preflight(Run)` skips a repair the job budget cannot pay for. D189 and the CHANGELOG give the worst case from the code (up to 3 producer runs per round, so 6; up to 4 verifier runs), labelled an estimate; the extra wall time, cost per repaired job and the share of D43-only repairs are not measured.

risks.risk: A round-two stop before a verdict loses round one's verdict, candidate or files, or leaves round two's progress note, kept-work directory or resume mark.
risks.mitigation: Round one's candidate, Verification, happened state and files are cloned before round two and restored when round two returns Ok with no Verification; round two's kept-work directory is removed; the mark was removed before round two and `settle_resume_marks` removes any later one for a Rejected job. The three stop cases and the direct restore test cover it. A hold (error return) keeps the existing hold behaviour.

risks.risk: Recognising Athena's own findings by text can drift if `judge`'s wording changes.
risks.mitigation: The not-assessed evidence and misread summary are shared consts used by `judge`; the two `format!` findings are matched by prefix and suffix consts and `repair_recognisers_match_what_judge_writes` runs the real `judge` for each, so a wording change fails a test instead of silently starting or stopping repairs.

risks.risk: The same failure class can still occur on a resumed-candidate path, a nested run, or a job whose budget or disk cannot pay for round two.
risks.mitigation: Not repaired and said so in D189 and the CHANGELOG; the budget and disk skips print a `repair     skipped:` line so the stored event shows the repair was considered. Extending to resumed candidates needs a producer snapshot and worktree guard in the resume path, a separate change.

risks.risk: The verifier's findings may be wrong, so a repair can churn the work.
risks.mitigation: The repair only gives information; the verdict is still computed by `judge`, unchanged. The always-fail bound test shows a stubborn verifier ends after one extra round. Misread-only, unassessed-only and (when the verifier passed) D43-only verdicts spend no round.

risks.risk: Throughput's check minutes and busy time read slightly low for repaired jobs, because round two's checks replace round one's in the stored Verification.
risks.mitigation: D189 and the CHANGELOG say so; the landing test pins first_pass == 0 and both rounds' producer and verifier minutes.

demonstrations.method: Same entry, fixture and wrapper as criterion 2. Case A: verdicts = [fail with an unmet criterion and a major finding] repeated. Case B: verdicts = [base pass]. Case C: a verdict whose only blocking item is a request misread (`request_misread: true`) with criteria met. Case D: a verdict whose criteria list is empty so the criterion is unassessed, with no other finding. `Counts` and the `Lines` sink are read after `go`. The pure cases run against the real `judge` (a `Verification` built by `judge_with_tree` from `VerdictInputs`, verify.rs:409) in unit tests named `repair_view_*`: unmet criterion; major finding; blocker from a held replay; failing check plus the verifier's unmet check criterion (Some); failing check with criterion marked met and no finding (None); D43-only with the verifier's verdict Pass (Behavior criterion met:true with no commands, None); D43-only with the verifier's verdict Fail (Some, listing the D43 criterion and finding); D43 plus a verifier major finding with verdict Pass (Some with only the finding); unassessed-only (None); misread-only (None); misread plus an unmet criterion (Some with only the criterion); timeout and incomplete verifier (None); minor-only (None); pass (None). `repair_recognisers_match_what_judge_writes` builds verdicts with the real `judge` for the not-assessed, D43 and misread cases and asserts each Athena finding is recognised by the consts and that the not-assessed evidence equals `NOT_ASSESSED_EVIDENCE`.

The `repair_view_*` unit tests return the values listed, including Some for a D43-only item when the verifier's verdict is Fail and None when it is Pass. demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `VERIFIER_REPAIRS` bound an always-failing verifier gives a third producer run or a loop, and counts (2,2) fail. Without the `repair_view` gate, the misread-only and unassessed-only verdicts would start a second producer run and counts (1,1) fail; case B guards that nothing extra runs when nothing is unmet. If `judge` changes a text a recogniser relies on, `repair_recognisers_match_what_judge_writes` fails.

demonstrations.method: Same entry and wrapper as criterion 2, run through `go` and `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head()?)` (tests.rs:2597-2599). (a) verdicts = [fail with CRITERION unmet and a major finding FIRST-CANARY, pass]. (b) verdicts = [that fail, fail with CRITERION met and a different major finding SECOND-CANARY]; the wrapper intercepts the introspection call (system prompt starts `You write one introspection`, as athena-cli tests/introspection.rs:31 and 52-72 do), keeps `event.what` from the user prompt JSON and returns an error turn; `go_with_stages` runs `introspect_job` on a Rejected job (mod.rs:430-436). A second check with four first-round items checks all four are in the reason. (c) verdicts = [that fail] and the second Producer call is overridden, in three cases, the way `producer_ending` (tests.rs:7424-7445) overrides a turn: (c1) `FakeTurn::output(json!("not a report"))`, which fails `ProducerOutput` parsing (producer.rs:448-457); (c2) `outcome = InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` with an edit (producer.rs:407; the pattern at tests.rs:7343); (c3) an error turn whose detail is `expired_login()` (tests.rs:7449). The second producer call also reads the job's resume mark from a `StateDir` over the same state path (`read_resume`, state.rs:309) and records it. `first_round_restore_puts_back_round_ones_files` builds a `Closing` through the constructor at mod.rs:294-309, pushes round one's replay and brief files, takes `FirstRound`, replaces them with `put_file`, adds a progress note, restores, and asserts `files` equals round one's. Nothing is faked except the agent turns and the mark read.

demonstrations.observes: (a) Invocation roles by seq are Reader, Producer, Verifier, Producer, Verifier. The first Verifier's `detail` holds the CRITERION text, FIRST-CANARY and `sent back to the producer for one repair pass`; the second has no detail and `verification.verifier_invocation` is its seq. In the UI lines, the first `verifier   ... fail` line comes before the `repair     ` line, then a second `producer   ` line, then the final `verifier   ... pass` line, all before the closing line. Final verdict Pass. (b) The outcome reason starts `the final verdict is fail:` and holds FIRST-CANARY, the CRITERION text, `one repair pass`, the first candidate's short commit and the invocation numbers; `event.what` holds the reason, FIRST-CANARY (first round only) and SECOND-CANARY (second verification); with four first-round items all four are in the reason. (c1, c2, c3) State Rejected, not Failed or TimedOut; `!is_environment_reason(&done.reason)`; the stored Verification is round one's (`verifier_invocation` is the first verifier's seq; `candidate_commit` equals `candidate.json`'s commit); `tree_retry_seed(&records, "try again on <job>", &redactor)` is Some with that commit and FIRST-CANARY in `must_address`; the reason holds the round-two stop reason, `the repair pass stopped before a verdict` and the note; the mark seen from round two is None and none remains after close; `job.briefs` has no `progress-note`; `kept_work_dir(&id)` does not exist; the stored `brief-verifier.md` and replay record are round one's. The job closes through `go`, so the closing commit passed `gate`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the repair step removed (the pre-change tree), the stored job has one verifier invocation with no detail and no second producer or verifier, so the ordered-roles, detail, UI-order and introspector-prompt assertions fail and `cargo test -p athena-core` on the pre-change tree fails on these tests. Without the restore, test (c) closes Failed or TimedOut with no Verification and `tree_retry_seed` returns None; without restoring `files` the progress note stays and the restore unit test fails; without the resume-mark removal the mark seen from round two is Some.
